memory_update.text: LRN is the highest-purity US-listed candidate for the K-12 virtual schooling and career-pathway node because it combines virtual school operations, long-duration school-as-a-service contracts, curriculum, LMS, support services, and middle/high-school career pathways.
PSO is a second direct operator/supplier through Pearson Virtual Learning and Connections Academy, but exposure is diluted by the broader Pearson portfolio.

The apparent chokepoint is public authorization plus durable school/district contracts and outcomes credibility; digital curriculum alone is less scarce because many curriculum vendors are private, nonprofit, or commoditized.
TYL and GOOGL are infrastructure mappings, not pure plays: they support K-12 administrative and device/platform capacity, but stock-level sensitivity to this node may be low.

Important private or nonprofit competitors/suppliers remain outside the US-listed universe: PowerSchool/Instructure status needs re-checking after privatization activity, and major K-12 assessment/curriculum entities such as College Board, ETS, NWEA, Curriculum Associates, Renaissance, HMH, Infinite Campus, and Edmentum are not clean US-listed public equities.

Need a later pass on regulated funding and policy risk: charter authorizers, state virtual-school caps, attendance rules, tutoring funding after pandemic-relief rolloff, and evidence standards for high-dosage tutoring could be the true gating variables.
